links.outcome: Whether adding multidisciplinary-team multiagent layer improves LLM AUC over single-agent settings
links.effect: MDT with in-context learning GPT-5 had AUC 0.8419 vs unaided baseline (P=.006), but adding MDT within matched settings did not significantly improve AUC over single-agent settings in either cohort.
links.quote: Although this configuration showed a significantly higher AUC than the fully unaided GPT-5 baseline (P=.006), this improvement reflected the combined effect of MDT and in-context learning, as adding the MDT framework within matched settings did not significantly improve AUC over corresponding single-agent settings in either cohort.

links.outcome: LLM configurations compared against traditional ML models and single-agent LLMs on same data
links.effect: Best GPT-5 MDT+ICL AUC 0.8419 vs random forest AUC 0.7857 internal validation; difference not significant (P=.18).
links.quote: The AUC of GPT-5 with MDT and in-context learning was also not significantly higher than that of the random forest model (P=.18).

screen.reason: The study empirically tests LLM predictive risk assessment by comparing performance with and without specific deployment/prompting practices (population-level in-context learning and multi-agent multidisciplinary team structured prompting) across retrospective and prospective cohorts.
